research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in lineup role coverage
separability of role coverage from talent and player counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and roster counts once talent is controlled?
Does talent control behave (no residual collinearity or over-adjustment) when coverage is measured per lineup within team?
What sample size and exposure are needed for stable within-team lineup coverage estimates across 90 team-seasons?

historical_evidence.finding: Fragility confirmatory test. Structural influence was reported as not reducible to usage (F1a residual-share about 0.90 to 0.93, CIs excluding low values). Split-half residual influence was reported as reproducible (F1b pooled-residual rho about +0.67 to +0.69). Record notes limited measurement reliability (LIM:low_measurement_reliability; RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY).

Wiring confirmatory test. Team offensive association structure was reported as persistent across split halves (Frobenius S about 0.35) and as retaining similarity after residualising play-type rates (residual R2 about 0.043). This concerns team-level association structure, not lineup role coverage.

Absence validation. Gate G2 passed (21/23 above null median) and V1(a) passed (16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16). The V2 prediction of absence-effect magnitude failed (V2a rho +0.288, p=0.077, CI spanning zero). Record notes LIM:small_sample.

Player-routing test. The A5 vs A3 signal fell from +0.94 pts/100 (V5) to +0.03 pts/100 on a 520-matchup sample (V6). The record classifies it as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Effects in this family shrank as sample size grew.

TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games. Player-channel lifts were large on small cells (e.g. n_def 15 to 28), while team-level lifts were small. Record classifies the question as A_unanswerable with LIM:insufficient_exposure and RISK:EXPOSURE_SPARSITY.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Lineup-cell PPP gaps were reported for named stars (cells n about 30 to 59). The record states no placebo or matching was done and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

Sequential suppression by the preceding opponent play. A PUTBACK effect was reported for several stars, with n_after as low as 30 to 32 in some cells. The record states there was no multiplicity correction and that some cells were small against thousands of baseline possessions.

Superstar suppression profiles. The Q5c verdict was that the rank-1 suppressor varies across players, but most rank-1 deltas were within 1 to 2 SE with no multiple-comparison control. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Playoff adaptation-pair sustainability (74 matchups). Pairs with enough signal were recorded as PIVOT_LOSES, and most population deltas were under 0.10. Record classifies the outcome as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null) with LIM:small_sample.

Sequence-memory horizon test on 1,024,980 possessions with a 2025-26 time-split. Short-memory horizon of about 2 to 3 possessions was supported, with most gain at lag 1 and absolute AUC about 0.591. This is a possession-level outcome study, not a coverage test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Routing possessions to each play type's best player as added value over a baseline, including after defensive-attention adaptation
failed_approaches.why: Recorded effect shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 when the matchup sample grew to 520; record classifies it as a powered null (B_powered_null). Scored outcomes were model-based, not observed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup decomposition of a TOV_FORCE lever into defender x initiator x play-type channels on four games
failed_approaches.why: Player-channel cells were small (n_def often 15 to 28) and attribution included helper steals; record classifies it as A_unanswerable with EXPOSURE_SPARSITY.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star-specific lineup and forced-play-type suppressors identified without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: Record states no placebo or matching and that later work treated similar gaps as artifacts; mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequential opponent-play suppression effects for individual stars
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction recorded; several cells had n_after of 30 to 32, which the record flags as thin against baseline possessions.
Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1 to 2 SE with no multiple-comparison control; recorded as inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: Within this project's retrieved records, talent-residual and reproducibility methods have been applied to team and player structure: FAM:SF18 reports residual influence that is not reducible to usage, and FAM:SF17 reports split-half persistence of team association structure. These show the general approach can be run on this data family.

Small-cell lineup and play-type contrasts in this project have repeatedly shrunk or failed to survive multiplicity control, placebo checks or holdout (FAM:SF-APPA-017, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-066).

The data family supports large possession counts (FAM:SF-APPS-059 used 1,024,980 possessions), but per-lineup and per-role cells are much smaller, and the retrieved records flag exposure sparsity at that level.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record defines organizer, shaper or terminal roles, measures lineup role coverage, or tests whether coverage varies within team.
No retrieved record tests separability of role coverage from talent and counts, or the behaviour of talent control for this measure.
No retrieved record gives a power calculation or minimum exposure for lineup role coverage across 90 team-seasons.
The retrieved records do not show whether role labels are defined independently of the outcome they are later used to predict.
own_inferences: The retrieved records are adjacent rather than direct. They support the general feasibility of talent-residual and holdout designs but do not answer the question as posed.
Lineup-level role coverage is likely to be collinear with talent (starter quality and usage) and with roster counts, so separability needs a pre-specified incremental test on held-out seasons.
Within-team variation in coverage may be small relative to lineup-level noise at 90 team-seasons, which would make a separability test underpowered unless the lineup threshold is high.

The pattern across FAM:SF-APPA-017, FAM:SF-APPM-054 and FAM:SF-APPA-066 suggests that effects found on small cells are likely to shrink under larger samples, so the design should use a pre-registered holdout season.
uncertainties: Exact definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal are not in the task statement or retrieved records, so the measure's construction and its reliability cannot be assessed.
Whether role labels are derived from the same play-by-play that defines lineup outcomes (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL risk) is unknown.
The 2025-26 regular season is only complete from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs only from 2026-06-21. Data version and the usable holdout depend on the access date.
The retrieval returned no record for the target question, so prior work coverage is unknown beyond the adjacent families.
The ratio of lineups meeting a minimum-possession threshold to all lineups within team-seasons is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: Without retrieved evidence the question would still need a design. The retrieved records show repeated failures of small-cell, unplaced, uncorrected lineup and play-type contrasts (FAM:SF-APPA-017, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-066). They also show residual-influence methods that survived holdout (FAM:SF18, FAM:SF17). Together these changed the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes: the test needs a pre-registered minimum lineup exposure, a talent measure built on disjoint seasons, a placebo role check, multiplicity control, and a 2025-26 holdout.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup-by-role cells within team-seasons may be too small for stable coverage estimates; FAM:SF-APPA-066 recorded cell n of 15 to 54 with insufficient exposure.
Separability of coverage from talent across 90 team-seasons may be underpowered; FAM:SF-APPM-054 and FAM:SF-APPS-059 flag small-sample and power limits in this data family.
FAM:SF18 records low measurement reliability as a limitation; the reliability of role-coverage measures is untested.
Coverage is plausibly collinear with talent and roster size, so separability depends on the talent measure and its construction.
If role labels are derived from outcomes or play-type points in the same possessions used to measure influence, the coverage measure would be partly defined by the outcome.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses lineup coverage of organizer, shaper or terminal roles, within-team variation, or separability from talent and counts. The cited records are adjacent: they cover residual influence and reproducibility (FAM:SF18, FAM:SF17), absence validation (FAM:SF20), and several small-cell lineup, play-type and routing contrasts that were flagged for exposure, multiplicity, placebo or power problems (FAM:SF-APPA-017, FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPM-054). FAM:SF-APPS-059 is a possession-level sequence study used as data-scale context.

risks.text: Per-lineup, per-role cells within team-seasons may be small. Set a pre-registered minimum-possession threshold and report the share of possessions retained.
Separability tests across 90 team-seasons may be underpowered. Compute minimum detectable incremental R2 by simulation before analysis.
Role coverage and talent measures may be noisy. Estimate split-half reliability of coverage before using it as a predictor.
Lineups or stints selected for extreme coverage may regress toward the mean. Use a pre-specified selection rule and a holdout season.
If organizer, shaper or terminal labels depend on the same points or outcomes used as the dependent variable, the separability test is circular. Define labels from pre-outcome features only.
Talent or role measures computed on the same season as the outcome leak information. Build talent from disjoint seasons.
Coverage is plausibly collinear with talent, usage and roster size. Test incremental contribution after talent and counts, not raw correlation.
Star-level findings in this family relied on uncontrolled comparisons (FAM:SF-CHT-009). Require placebo role labels and matched comparisons.
Several roles and lineup cells invite many tests; FAM:SF-APPA-050 and FAM:SF-APPM-022 lacked correction. Apply Holm correction across roles.
Role usage and team strategy change across seasons; FAM:SF-APPA-050 carries a drift risk flag. Use season-blocked splits.
Lineup PPP differences are small relative to baseline variance, so the effect may be near zero. Report effect sizes with intervals against a talent-only baseline.

design.estimand: Incremental association between within-team lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper or terminal on court) and lineup-level offensive efficiency (PPP), conditional on out-of-season talent and roster counts, with separability reported as the increment in held-out R2 over a talent-and-counts baseline.
design.unit: Lineup-stint within team-season, restricted to lineup-stints meeting the pre-registered possession threshold. Role labels are assigned from pre-outcome features only.
design.sample: Discovery: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons (90 team-seasons total across all available seasons, per the data description). Holdout: 2025-26 regular season, used once and only from its complete-data version (from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are excluded from the primary test and reported as a secondary check.
design.power: Before analysis, simulate the minimum detectable incremental held-out R2 at the chosen possession threshold and at 90 team-seasons, and pre-register the threshold. If the detectable effect is below a practically relevant size, report the question as underpowered rather than null.
design.controls: Talent measured from player ratings fitted on disjoint seasons (no same-season outcome leakage). Controls for roster counts, minutes, opponent strength, and game state. Within-team fixed effects. Report variance inflation factors for coverage against talent and counts.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo role labels assigned by permutation within team-season should show no incremental R2. (2) Coverage should not predict a non-role outcome such as defensive rebound share. (3) Separability must hold on the 2025-26 holdout, not only in discovery.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across the three roles and the all-role coverage indicator. Pre-register the family of tests before running any analysis.
design.decision_rule: Separability is supported only if the incremental held-out R2 of coverage over the talent-and-counts baseline is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero after Holm correction, in the 2025-26 holdout, and the placebo labels show no incremental R2. If the power check shows the detectable effect is too large, report underpowered. Otherwise a null is reported as a null.
design.data_version: Per-game files from the NBA stats API as of 2026-07-13: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 (partial before). Derived play-type possession graph built from the play-by-play, with its build date recorded. Units: 420,993 possessions and 90 team-seasons as recorded.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
